🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-16 23:00 → 2026-09-17 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Conformance loop closed fast** — A reviewer named the missing negative test, the author pushed the fix in the same session, and CI turned green. [PR #42](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/42)

> **Mutation-survival layer opened** — A new PR introduces a discipline requiring every test to catch its targeted mutation, making the suite genuinely load-bearing. [PR #17](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/17)

> **DAO Fund mechanics and build sequencing aligned** — The fund flow was sketched end-to-end and the group confirmed which builds stay active versus stay at scoping. [tg:tawg:4736]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### recompute-kit conformance

_Conformance work across several PRs and an independent cold verification advanced test integrity and extended coverage into new authorization and admission profiles._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Closed** the profile-commitment-loop PR after chaining both ends of the commitment model into one mechanical seam, giving the group a stable anchor for conformance tests that rely on this boundary. [PR #42](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/42)

- Baby Blue Viper **Identified** the sixth case as a load-bearing negative rather than optional coverage, giving Merlini a precise target that converted an open concern into a closed item in the same session. [PR #42 comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/42#issuecomment-5720577018)

- Merlini (@gobross) **Added** the sixth test vector and pushed commit 0f9c4ed with CI green, completing the review-to-fix loop and showing how fast a precisely named gap can be resolved. [PR #42 comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/42#issuecomment-5720703428)

- Merlini (@gobross) **Opened** the recompute-mutation-survival PR to introduce a discipline requiring each test to catch a targeted mutation, raising the quality bar for all future conformance work. [PR #17](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/17)

- Pavlo **Opened** a conformance PR separating event-time and concurrent admission safety into distinct profiles, making each failure mode independently falsifiable and easier to maintain without cross-contamination. [PR #45](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/45)

- Zexo **Verified** the PR #45 profile cold at a pinned commit, confirming all assertions and mutation targets held across both test sets, and flagged a predicate scope boundary for the author to evaluate. [PR #45 comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/45#issuecomment-5713514281)

- Pavlo **Opened** a second conformance PR binding event authorization to consumption-time state, extending coverage into an authorization gap the existing profiles left open. [PR #46](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/pull/46)

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Explained** in chat why keeping the failure-mode distinction is worthwhile: it makes each mode independently falsifiable, the precise quality that makes the separation across both new profiles defensible. [tg:tawg:4723]

### ERC-8004

_A forum exchange sharpened a previously under-stated gap, giving editors a cleaner target._

- A forum contributor **Surfaced** the sharpest formulation yet of an under-stated gap in the spec, helping the authoring group name exactly what was missing and pointing toward a more precise revision. [ERC-8004 forum](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/400)

### organization

_The group aligned on fund mechanics and confirmed build sequencing._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Shared** a structured sketch of the DAO Fund flow — RFPs posted on a board, backers pledge and pay when fully funded, and a 30-day build-proposal window opens — giving the group a common mechanics model to plan around. [tg:tawg:4736]

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Confirmed** build sequencing: Robinhood stays the active build focus and Spec Bank remains at scoping until real bandwidth appears, and committed to starting a deliverable-to-existing-asset map to make handoffs concrete. [tg:tawg:4740]

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Claimed** the lead on Track C (deterministic PoC triage) in the DAO Fund list, connecting the track to ongoing test-writing work and moving it from unassigned to actively owned. [tg:tawg:4741]

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Offered** to create the Track C topic and invited Zexo to reach out anytime, removing a coordination gap that could otherwise slow the track from getting started. [tg:tawg:4743]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Whether the deliverable-to-asset map will surface dependencies that affect the Robinhood build timeline
- Whether the predicate scope boundary Zexo flagged in the PR #45 review warrants its own conformance profile
- How the DAO Fund mechanics sketch evolves into a repeatable RFP template

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Baby Blue Viper: complete the rough deliverable-to-existing-asset map for Robinhood
- Zexo: start Track C and use the topic Jimmy Shi offered to create
- Review PR #45 and PR #46 for merge readiness
- PR #17 needs a review pass to confirm the mutation-survival discipline is complete

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A reviewer named the exact gap, the fix landed in the same session, and CI confirmed it — the review-to-close loop ran without anyone leaving the thread.
>
> Keep handing the work forward like this — when the thread stays live, gaps close before they can fossilize. 🔗
